changes_made.explanation: Removed duplicate 'pseudo captions' from outputs. The paper does generate pseudo-captions via Rel2Cap, which qualifies as NLG.

Changed answer from Yes to No. CLIP-Score is used to measure data quality of retrieved/generated pairs, not to evaluate the quality of generated text. The paper does not use automatic NLG evaluation metrics.
No LLM-as-judge evaluation is used in this paper.
No human evaluation of generated outputs is conducted in this paper.

overall_notes: This paper is primarily about vision-and-language pre-training using relative representations. While it does generate pseudo-captions (NLG), the main evaluation is on downstream V+L understanding tasks, not on the quality of generated text. The extracted metadata was mostly accurate, but CLIP-Score was incorrectly categorized as an NLG evaluation metric when it's actually used for data quality assessment.
